cards.title: Even numbers leave nothing over
cards.body: A number is even when dividing it by 2 leaves no remainder, so `n % 2` is `0`.

hi.title: Even numbers mein kuch nahi bachta
hi.body: Number even hota hai jab 2 se divide karne par koi remainder nahi bachta, yaani `n % 2` ka matlab `0`.

cards.title: == compares, = stores
cards.body: `=` puts a value into a variable. `==` asks whether two values are equal. Inside an `if`, you almost always want `==`.

hi.title: == compare karta hai, = store karta hai
hi.body: `=` variable mein value daalta hai. `==` poochta hai ki do values barabar hain ya nahi. `if` ke andar almost hamesha `==` chahiye.

cards.title: Spot the bug
cards.body: It should check whether a number divides by 5, but Python refuses to run it. Tap the bug.

bug.fix: `=` stores a value; `==` compares two. Line 2 needs `n % 5 == 0`.

hi.title: Bug dhoondo
hi.body: Isse check karna chahiye ki number 5 se divide hota hai ya nahi, par Python ise chalane se mana kar deta hai. Bug par tap karo.
hi.fix: `=` value store karta hai; `==` do values compare karta hai. Line 2 ko `n % 5 == 0` chahiye.

check.question: What does this print?
check.explanation: 15 % 2 is 1, and 1 == 0 is False, so 15 is odd.

hi.question: Yeh kya print karega?
hi.explanation: 15 % 2 ka matlab 1, aur 1 == 0 False hai, isliye 15 odd hai.

exercise.prompt: Read a whole number and print `even` if it divides by 2 with nothing left over, otherwise print `odd`.
exercise.promptHi: Ek whole number padho aur agar woh 2 se poora divide hota hai toh `even` print karo, warna `odd`.

n = int(input())
# print even or odd below
